Reddit announced two upcoming changes that may upset some long-time users.

The company has already placed one restriction on old Reddit, and now a second one. Additionally, RSS support is also being discontinued...

Old Reddit

Reddit underwent a major user interface change in 2018, which was strongly opposed by users who preferred the original version. In response, the platform pledged at the time to continue offering the old version of Reddit (now referred to as Old Reddit) for as long as people were still using it.

In August this year, the company implemented its first policy change, requiring users of old Reddit to log in. Now they are further announcing that the original UI will only be available to users who have used it within the past six months, and new users who have never used it will no longer be able to log in.

Reddit says both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping of content by the company (though word is that paying can get you an exception).

RSS subscription feature to be discontinued

The reason for discontinuing RSS subscriptions is the same.

This change may cause significant problems for subreddits that rely on RSS for moderation work. Reddit says it understands the situation and suggests moderators switch to Devvit applications, such as Discord Relay.

User reaction is lukewarm

Judging from the discussion in the comments section, many long-time users are very dissatisfied with the recent changes.

What do you think of these changes? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
